questions.question: The approach under the E-Waste (Management) Rules in which the producer is made responsible for the collection and environmentally sound management of its product at the end of its life is called:
questions.explanation: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) makes the producer responsible for the product up to its end-of-life stage. It was introduced in the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016 and strengthened with EPR certificates in the 2022 Rules.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 came into force on:
questions.explanation: The 2022 Rules were notified in November 2022 and came into force on 1 April 2023, replacing the 2016 Rules.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which mechanism introduced by the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 allows a producer to meet its EPR target through certificates generated by registered recyclers and refurbishers?
questions.explanation: Under the 2022 Rules, recyclers and refurbishers generate EPR certificates on the basis of the e-waste they process, and producers buy them to fulfil their EPR obligation.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: In the E-Waste Rules, a person who restores used electrical and electronic equipment to working condition for resale is known as a:
questions.explanation: A refurbisher restores used equipment to working order. A dismantler takes equipment apart into components, and a recycler recovers materials from the components.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Registration of producers, manufacturers, recyclers and refurbishers under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 is done through an online portal operated by the:
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.explanation: The Central Pollution Control Board runs the portal for registration, EPR certificates and filing of returns under the 2022 Rules.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The metal present in the backlight lamps and switches of old electronic equipment that caused the Minamata disease is:
questions.explanation: Mercury, as methylmercury, caused Minamata disease (Japan). In e-waste mercury occurs in flat-panel backlights, switches and relays.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Chronic exposure to cadmium from e-waste components such as rechargeable batteries mainly damages the:
questions.explanation: Cadmium accumulates in the kidneys and causes bone demineralisation (itai-itai disease). Nickel-cadmium batteries and some semiconductors are common sources in e-waste.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Burning of cables and plastics containing brominated flame retardants at low temperature in open air releases highly toxic:
questions.explanation: Incomplete combustion of halogenated plastics (PVC, brominated flame retardants) produces polychlorinated/polybrominated dioxins and furans, which are persistent and carcinogenic.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which technique is used to separate non-ferrous metals such as aluminium and copper from non-metallic fractions of shredded e-waste?
questions.explanation: An eddy current separator repels conducting non-ferrous metals from a moving stream, whereas a magnetic separator removes only ferrous metals.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about mechanical processing of e-waste:
1. Magnetic separators remove ferrous metals.
2. Eddy current separators recover non-ferrous metals.
3. Density separation can separate plastics from metals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are standard unit operations in e-waste pre-processing: magnetic separation for ferrous metals, eddy current for non-ferrous metals and density (air or water) separation for plastics and metals.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Recovery of metals from e-waste by dissolving them in acid or other lixiviants and then recovering them from the solution is called:
questions.explanation: Hydrometallurgy uses aqueous leaching followed by precipitation, solvent extraction or electrowinning. Pyrometallurgy uses high-temperature smelting.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Use of bacteria such as Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans to solubilise metals from e-waste is known as:
questions.explanation: Bioleaching uses acidophilic microbes to oxidise and dissolve metals such as copper, and is an eco-friendly alternative to cyanide or strong-acid leaching.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which of the following precious metals is commonly recovered from printed circuit boards of discarded electronics?
questions.explanation: Printed circuit boards contain gold, silver, palladium and copper, in higher concentration than most natural ores, which is why e-waste is called an 'urban mine'.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The term 'urban mining' refers to:
options: Mining of sand from urban rivers
Recovering valuable metals and materials from e-waste and other urban waste stocks
questions.explanation: Urban mining recovers metals such as copper, gold and rare earths from discarded products, reducing the need for virgin mining.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Basel Convention regulates:
options: Substances that deplete the ozone layer
Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes and their disposal
questions.explanation: The Basel Convention (adopted 1989, in force 1992) controls the export and import of hazardous wastes, including e-waste, to prevent dumping in developing countries.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which convention prohibits the import of hazardous wastes into African countries?
questions.explanation: The Bamako Convention (1991) bans the import of hazardous and radioactive waste into Africa and regulates its movement within the continent.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The European Union directive that restricts the use of lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, PBB and PBDE in electrical and electronic equipment is abbreviated as:
questions.explanation: RoHS (Restriction of Hazardous Substances) limits these six substances. India's E-Waste Rules also contain RoHS-type restrictions on the same substances.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Brominated flame retardants (PBDEs) used in the plastics of electronic goods are regulated internationally as persistent organic pollutants under the:
questions.explanation: Several PBDEs were listed as POPs under the Stockholm Convention in 2009 because they are persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A major challenge in managing e-waste in India is that a large share of it is handled by:
questions.explanation: Informal workers dismantle and recycle most e-waste using acid baths and open burning, which harms health and the environment and wastes recoverable materials.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A scheme in which the producer charges an additional amount at the time of sale and returns it to the consumer when the end-of-life product is handed back is known as the:
questions.explanation: The Deposit Refund Scheme was one of the EPR instruments allowed under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2016.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: In the E-Waste Rules, a Producer Responsibility Organisation (PRO) is:
options: An organisation set up by producers to take back and manage e-waste on their behalf
A government authority that fixes recycling rates
A trade union of informal recyclers
A body that certifies electronic products
questions.explanation: A PRO is a professional body, financed collectively by producers, that arranges collection, channelisation and recycling of e-waste for its members.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which practice directly increases the quantity of e-waste generated?
questions.explanation: Designing products for a short life or making them impossible to upgrade shortens use time and increases e-waste. Repair, modular design and take-back reduce it.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Open burning of waste cables to recover copper is harmful to health.
Reason (R): Burning of plastic-coated cables releases dioxins, furans and heavy-metal fumes.
Select the correct answer.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The harm to health arises because the burning of the plastic coating releases toxic dioxins, furans and metal fumes, so R explains A.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Arrange the following e-waste management options from the MOST preferred to the LEAST preferred:
1. Recycling of materials
2. Reuse and refurbishment
3. Safe disposal in a secure landfill
4. Prevention and reduction at source
questions.explanation: The waste hierarchy runs prevention, reuse/refurbishment, recycling, recovery and finally disposal.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Lead : Impaired neurological development :: Cadmium : ?
questions.explanation: Lead mainly harms the nervous system, especially in children. Cadmium accumulates in the kidneys and damages them.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Match the hazardous substance in e-waste (Column I) with its main health effect (Column II).
Column I: A. Lead  B. Mercury  C. Cadmium  D. Beryllium
Column II: 1. Kidney damage and itai-itai disease  2. Chronic lung disease (berylliosis)  3. Impaired cognitive development in children  4. Minamata disease
questions.explanation: Lead damages the developing brain, mercury causes Minamata disease, cadmium damages kidneys and bones, and beryllium dust causes berylliosis.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: As per the E-Waste Rules, the term 'e-waste' includes:
options: Only equipment that contains no hazardous substances
Components, consumables, parts and spares of electrical and electronic equipment discarded as waste, and rejects from manufacturing, refurbishment and repair
Only waste generated by government offices
Only fully assembled computers and mobile phones discarded by households
questions.explanation: The legal definition covers whole equipment as well as components, spares and process rejects, whether discarded by consumers, bulk consumers or industry.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Compared with natural ores, printed circuit boards of discarded electronics typically contain:
options: A lower concentration of all metals
A much higher concentration of gold and copper per tonne
questions.explanation: The gold and copper content of circuit boards per tonne is many times that of typical ores, which makes e-waste recycling economically attractive when done safely.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The National Policy for Management of Crop Residues (2014) was formulated by the:
options: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation: The policy promotes in-situ management with machinery, ex-situ uses such as fodder and energy, and discourages open burning.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A machine fitted to a combine harvester that chops paddy straw and spreads it uniformly in the field is called a:
questions.explanation: The Super SMS spreads chopped straw evenly so that wheat can be sown with a Happy Seeder or Super Seeder without burning the residue.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which machine compresses loose straw into compact bundles that are removed from the field for ex-situ use?
questions.explanation: Balers form rectangular or round bales of straw, which are used as fuel in biomass plants, as fodder or as industrial feedstock.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Pusa Bio-decomposer used to hasten the decomposition of paddy straw in the field was developed by:
options: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi
questions.explanation: The Pusa Decomposer is a consortium of fungal strains, given as capsules or a prepared solution, and speeds up decomposition of rice straw into manure.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The main reason farmers in Punjab and Haryana burn paddy straw is:
options: Paddy straw has high market value as fodder
Law makes burning compulsory for pest control
The very short gap between paddy harvest and sowing of the wheat crop
questions.explanation: Late transplanting of paddy leaves only 2 to 3 weeks before wheat sowing, so farmers burn the straw as the quickest and cheapest way to clear the field.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which of the following is a direct effect of burning crop residue on soil?
options: Loss of organic carbon, nitrogen and beneficial soil microbes
questions.explanation: Burning heats the top soil, kills beneficial microbes and volatilises nitrogen and carbon, so the soil gradually becomes less fertile.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a significant pollutant released by open burning of crop residue?
questions.explanation: Crop residue burning releases CO, CO2, CH4, N2O, NOx, SO2 and fine particulates and black carbon. CFCs are industrial ozone-depleting chemicals, not products of biomass burning.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Ethanol produced from lignocellulosic crop residues such as paddy straw is called:
questions.explanation: First-generation ethanol comes from sugar or starch crops. Second-generation ethanol uses lignocellulosic residues such as straw, bagasse and stalks.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The SATAT initiative of the Government of India promotes the production and use of:
options: Compressed biogas (CBG) from agricultural residue, municipal waste and cattle dung
questions.explanation: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) encourages CBG plants that use waste and residues as feedstock, giving farmers an alternative to burning.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Biogas produced by anaerobic digestion of crop residue and animal dung consists mainly of:
questions.explanation: Biogas is about 55 to 65 per cent methane with the rest mainly carbon dioxide. The remaining slurry is a nutrient-rich manure.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which edible mushroom is commercially cultivated on paddy straw?
questions.explanation: The paddy straw mushroom (Volvariella volvacea) grows well on chopped, moist paddy straw in tropical regions, giving farmers a use for the residue.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Biochar is produced from crop residue by:
options: Pyrolysis, i.e. heating biomass in limited or no oxygen
questions.explanation: Pyrolysis converts biomass into stable, carbon-rich biochar, which stores carbon in soil for long periods and improves nutrient and water retention.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A major environmental benefit of applying biochar to soil is:
options: Rapid release of its carbon as CO2
Long-term carbon sequestration and better retention of water and nutrients
questions.explanation: Biochar is very resistant to decomposition, so the carbon stays in the soil for decades or centuries, while its porous structure holds water and nutrients.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The fibrous residue left after extraction of juice from sugarcane, widely used in sugar mills for generating power, is:
questions.explanation: Bagasse is burnt in cogeneration plants of sugar mills to produce steam and electricity, some of which is exported to the grid.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Rice husk ash can be used as a supplementary cementitious material because it is rich in:
questions.explanation: Rice husk burnt under controlled conditions gives ash with 85 to 95 per cent amorphous silica, which has pozzolanic activity.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Rice straw is a poor fodder for cattle mainly because of its:
options: High silica content and low palatability and digestibility
questions.explanation: Silica and lignin make rice straw hard to digest, so it has low nutritive value compared with wheat straw or legume residues.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: When crop residue with a very high carbon-to-nitrogen ratio is incorporated into the soil, microorganisms temporarily:
options: Fix atmospheric nitrogen in large amounts
questions.explanation: Microbes decomposing carbon-rich residues take up mineral nitrogen from the soil for their own growth, so crops may suffer nitrogen deficiency until the residue decomposes.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The ideal initial carbon-to-nitrogen ratio for efficient composting of organic waste is about:
questions.explanation: A C:N ratio of about 25-30:1 gives fast aerobic decomposition. Higher ratios slow it down, and lower ratios lose nitrogen as ammonia.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about crop residue management:
1. In-situ management includes mulching, incorporation and zero-tillage sowing.
2. Ex-situ management includes baling the straw for biomass energy or fodder.
3. Open burning in the field is the recommended practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Open burning is discouraged and banned in several states. In-situ and ex-situ options are the recommended ways of managing residue.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sowing wheat with a Happy Seeder into standing rice stubble helps conserve soil moisture.
Reason (R): The residue left on the surface acts as mulch and reduces evaporation.
Select the correct answer.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The straw retained as surface mulch reduces evaporation and soil temperature, so it explains the moisture saving.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), which deals with stubble burning, was set up under:
options: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 alone
The Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas Act, 2021
questions.explanation: CAQM was constituted by a 2021 statute and has powers to issue directions on matters such as crop residue burning in Delhi-NCR and adjoining states.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: In 2015 the order banning open burning of crop residue in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan was passed by the:
questions.explanation: The National Green Tribunal prohibited crop residue burning in 2015 and fixed environmental compensation to be paid by defaulting farmers.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: To reduce stubble burning, the Ministry of Power has promoted the use of crop residue in the power sector through:
options: Use of straw in hydroelectric turbines
Replacement of all coal by biomass in one year
Co-firing of biomass pellets with coal in thermal power plants
questions.explanation: A 2021 policy asked coal-based power plants to blend a minimum share of biomass pellets, made from agro-residue, with coal.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The earthworm species most commonly used in vermicomposting of crop residue and farm waste is:
questions.explanation: Eisenia fetida, the red wiggler or tiger worm, is an epigeic species that thrives in decomposing organic matter and is widely used in vermicomposting.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Compressing cotton stalks, groundnut shells and rice husk into dense blocks that are used as boiler fuel is called:
questions.explanation: Briquettes made from agricultural residue are a renewable solid fuel that replaces coal or firewood in boilers and brick kilns.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Arrange the phases of aerobic composting in the correct sequence:
1. Thermophilic phase
2. Mesophilic phase
3. Cooling (second mesophilic) phase
4. Maturation or curing phase
questions.explanation: Composting begins with mesophilic microbes, heats up to the thermophilic phase, then cools and finally matures into stable humus.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Match the item in Column I with its role in crop residue management in Column II.
Column I: A. Happy Seeder  B. Baler  C. Pusa Bio-decomposer  D. Biogas digester
Column II: 1. Sows wheat directly into residue  2. Makes compact bundles of straw  3. Speeds up microbial decomposition in the field  4. Converts residue into methane-rich gas
questions.explanation: The Happy Seeder is used for in-situ sowing, the baler for ex-situ removal, the Pusa Decomposer for in-field decomposition and the digester for biogas.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Paddy straw : In-situ incorporation :: Straw bales : ?
questions.explanation: Straw ploughed back into the field is in-situ management. Baled straw removed from the field is used ex situ, for example for energy or fodder.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which greenhouse gas is emitted in large quantities from continuously flooded rice fields, even without any burning?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in flooded paddy soil by methanogenic bacteria releases methane. Alternate wetting and drying or direct-seeded rice reduces it.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The term 'biodiversity' was coined in 1985 by:
questions.explanation: Walter G. Rosen coined the term 'biological diversity' for the 1986 National Forum on BioDiversity; E. O. Wilson helped to popularise it.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Pollination, flood control, climate regulation and nutrient cycling are examples of:
questions.explanation: These benefits are not consumed or sold directly, but ecosystems provide them, so they are indirect-use or ecosystem-service values.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: In the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment, climate regulation and flood control are classified as:
questions.explanation: Provisioning services supply goods such as food and water, regulating services control processes such as climate and floods, cultural services give recreation and spiritual benefits, and supporting services such as nutrient cycling underpin the others.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Timber : Productive use value :: Fuelwood collected by villagers : ?
questions.explanation: Products sold in the market give productive use value, whereas fuelwood, fodder and food used directly by local people give consumptive use value.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Wild relatives of crop plants are important for biodiversity conservation mainly because they:
options: Always give higher yields than cultivated varieties
Provide genes for pest resistance and stress tolerance for crop breeding
Replace the need for any gene banks
Fix atmospheric nitrogen in all soils
questions.explanation: Wild relatives hold genetic traits such as disease resistance and drought tolerance that breeders can introduce into crop varieties.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Match the sacred grove (Column I) with the region where it is found (Column II).
Column I: A. Kavu  B. Devrai  C. Orans  D. Law Kyntang
Column II: 1. Kerala  2. Maharashtra  3. Rajasthan  4. Meghalaya
questions.explanation: Sacred groves are patches of forest protected on religious grounds: Kavu in Kerala, Devrai in Maharashtra, Orans in Rajasthan and Law Kyntang in Meghalaya.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Appiko movement of 1983, which aimed to save forests by hugging trees, took place in:
questions.explanation: Appiko ('hugging' in Kannada) was started in Uttara Kannada district of Karnataka and was inspired by the Chipko movement of Uttarakhand.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan, who gave their lives in 1730 at Khejarli, were protecting:
questions.explanation: About 363 Bishnoi villagers died resisting the felling of khejri (Prosopis cineraria) trees. The community also protects blackbuck and chinkara.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: To qualify as a biodiversity hotspot, a region must have lost at least what proportion of its original natural vegetation?
questions.explanation: Conservation International's criteria are at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species and a loss of at least 70 per cent of the primary vegetation.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A region qualifies as a biodiversity hotspot only if it contains at least how many endemic species of vascular plants?
questions.explanation: At least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species, or 0.5 per cent of the world total, are needed, along with 70 per cent loss of original habitat.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: How many of the world's biodiversity hotspots occur in India?
questions.explanation: India has parts of four hotspots: the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which biodiversity hotspot includes the Nicobar Islands of India?
questions.explanation: The Nicobar Islands are part of the Sundaland hotspot, whereas the Andaman Islands fall within Indo-Burma.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Convention on Biological Diversity was opened for signature at the:
options: Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro, 1992
questions.explanation: The CBD was opened for signature at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and came into force in December 1993.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Nagoya Protocol to the Convention on Biological Diversity deals with:
options: Trade in endangered wild fauna and flora
Liability for oil spills at sea
Access to genetic resources and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their use
questions.explanation: The Nagoya Protocol (2010) on Access and Benefit Sharing is implemented in India through the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022) sets a target of protecting what share of the world's land and oceans by 2030?
questions.explanation: The '30 by 30' target was agreed at COP15 of the CBD in December 2022 and replaced the Aichi Targets (2011-2020).
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The headquarters of the National Biodiversity Authority, set up under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, is at:
questions.explanation: The NBA was established in 2003 at Chennai. State Biodiversity Boards and local Biodiversity Management Committees work under it.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, Biodiversity Management Committees are constituted by:
questions.explanation: Every local body must constitute a BMC to promote conservation and to prepare a People's Biodiversity Register in consultation with local people.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A People's Biodiversity Register documents:
options: Industrial pollution levels in a village
The population of all wildlife in national parks only
Prices of forest produce in local markets
Local biological resources and the associated traditional knowledge
questions.explanation: The register records the biological resources of a locality, their uses and traditional knowledge, and helps in protecting it from misappropriation.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which IUCN Red List category denotes the highest risk of extinction among the threatened categories?
questions.explanation: The threatened categories in decreasing order of risk are Critically Endangered, Endangered and Vulnerable.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A species whose impact on its ecosystem is much greater than its abundance would suggest is called a:
questions.explanation: Removal of a keystone species, such as a top predator or a fig tree in a tropical forest, causes large changes in the community.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: A charismatic species such as the tiger that is used to attract public and financial support for conservation is called a:
questions.explanation: Flagship species generate public interest, and protecting their habitat usually protects many other species as well.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Protecting a large-ranging species such as the tiger also protects many other species in its habitat. Such a species is known as an:
questions.explanation: An umbrella species needs a large area of intact habitat, so conserving it conserves the habitats and species that share the area.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
options: Gene bank of the National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources, New Delhi
questions.explanation: Ex-situ conservation protects species outside their natural habitat, for example in gene banks, seed banks, botanical gardens and zoos.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about biodiversity hotspots:
1. They are defined on the basis of species endemism and degree of threat.
2. India has parts of four hotspots.
3. All hotspots lie in tropical rainforests only.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Hotspots include Mediterranean, savanna and montane regions as well as rainforests, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Decline of pollinating insects threatens the production of many crops.
Reason (R): A large number of crop plants depend on animals for pollination.
Select the correct answer.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: Pollination by bees and other insects is essential for many fruits, vegetables and oilseeds, so pollinator decline directly reduces yields.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question:
Arrange the levels of biodiversity from the smallest to the largest scale:
1. Species diversity
2. Genetic diversity
3. Ecosystem diversity
questions.explanation: Biodiversity is studied at three levels: genetic diversity within species, species diversity within communities and diversity of ecosystems across landscapes.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes), which chokes lakes and canals in India, is an example of:
questions.explanation: Introduced from South America, water hyacinth multiplies rapidly, depletes oxygen in water bodies and harms native aquatic life. It was called the 'Terror of Bengal'.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary in Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh is known for the conservation of the:
questions.explanation: Rollapadu protects grassland habitat of the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard and the lesser florican.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Kolleru Lake, a Ramsar site known for migratory birds such as the spot-billed pelican, lies between the deltas of the rivers:
questions.explanation: Kolleru is a large freshwater lake in the Godavari-Krishna delta region of Andhra Pradesh and was designated a Ramsar site in 2002.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary in East Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh is mainly a:
options: Dry deciduous forest of the Nallamala hills
Mangrove forest in the Godavari estuary
questions.explanation: Coringa has the second largest stretch of mangroves in India and is home to the fishing cat and many water birds.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus), a threatened timber species, is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of:
questions.explanation: Red sanders grows naturally only in the Seshachalam and Nallamala hills of Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring tracts. It is listed in CITES Appendix II and its felling and trade are strictly regulated.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve, the largest tiger reserve in India by area, is spread over:
questions.explanation: The reserve covers parts of the Nallamala forest in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana along the Krishna river.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve in Andhra Pradesh is located in the districts of:
questions.explanation: The Seshachalam hills, which include Tirumala, form a biosphere reserve known for red sanders and endemic flora.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)

questions.question: The largest brackish-water lagoon of India, Chilika, is in Odisha. Which lagoon on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu is the second largest?
questions.explanation: Pulicat Lake, separated from the Bay of Bengal by the barrier island of Sriharikota, is famous for flamingos and other migratory birds.
questions.source: Team Civilians original · AEE PCB Paper-II pattern (APPSC 2025 and TGPSC 2026 papers studied)
